subject.title: Per-agent tools.selfDeny — allow tool inheritance to subagents while denying direct use

question: Should OpenClaw add a delegate-only/self-deny requester tool policy, and what public config shape should own that security boundary?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix adds public configuration and changes security-sensitive tool inheritance semantics between requester agents and subagents, which automation should not choose unilaterally.

options.title: Sponsor delegate-only config
options.body: Add a documented selfDeny/delegateOnly-style field with deny precedence, visibility diagnostics, and tests proving requester-hidden but child-inherited tools.

options.title: Fold into per-spawn policy
options.body: Keep this issue open until the per-spawn toolsAllow design grows into a broader capability model that also covers requester self-denial.

options.title: Reject new config surface
options.body: Document separate agent IDs or strict behavioral routing as the supported pattern, accepting that config-level separation of duties remains unavailable.

recommendation.title: Sponsor delegate-only config
recommendation.body: Add a documented selfDeny/delegateOnly-style field with deny precedence, visibility diagnostics, and tests proving requester-hidden but child-inherited tools.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest current-main and prior-review routing signal for this config/security boundary.
